mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in three consecutive weeks (3.7 to 0.6 to -4.4 to -13.3), reflecting strong negative momentum. Absent a reversal signal, this autocorrelated decline will persist, pulling the next-4-week mean below the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean exceeds its 4-week trailing mean despite the observed 3-week consecutive decline.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility crosses above +9 points for two consecutive weeks, it indicates intensified stay-at-home compliance consistent with tightened social-distancing policy, which mechanically suppresses discretionary retail and recreation trips over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 9.3 at t-0w, the highest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains flat over the subsequent 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL stayed above +9 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate reduced commuting-linked foot traffic; when both series fall together week-on-week, the compounded loss of transit-adjacent and workplace-adjacent retail spillover accelerates the RETAIL_REC decline beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -2.6 to -8.7 and WORKPLACES fell from 6.0 to -0.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's decline rate does not exceed the single-series baseline prediction in weeks where both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES co-decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions, a sustained decline in PARKS mobility signals curtailed outdoor recreational freedom that typically precedes or accompanies restrictions on indoor retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -4.4 to -16.7 over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean is higher than its trailing 4-week mean despite PARKS continuing a monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: A short-term calendar effect (e.g., approach of a public holiday period in Hong Kong) can produce a one-week rebound in discretionary shopping as households make pre-holiday purchases, temporarily reversing the downward RETAIL_REC trend within a one-week horizon even as the longer trend remains negative.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined sharply at t-0w to -13.3, a level consistent with a pre-holiday trough before rebound
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show any one-week uptick within the next 4 weeks relative to the t-0w trough.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated above +45 points while RETAIL_REC continues to fall, this indicates households are substituting discretionary retail trips with essential stockpiling behavior, a pattern that persists and keeps RETAIL_REC suppressed over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +45 for all four observed weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between 48.6 and 53.7 across all four weeks while RETAIL_REC fell
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers to positive growth over the next 4 weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above +45 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL combined with volatile, net-negative WORKPLACES mobility suggests expanded work-from-home mandates; the interaction of these two series reduces the frequency of out-of-home trips that would otherwise include retail stops, compounding the suppression of RETAIL_REC over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES is negative in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 9.3 while WORKPLACES was -0.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further in weeks where RESIDENTIAL rises concurrently with negative WORKPLACES readings.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in TRANSIT mobility over multiple weeks reflects reduced use of public transit infrastructure that normally feeds retail districts; in a steady-state (non-recovering) regime, this reduced transit flow directly lowers downstream retail footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from 3.3 to -8.7 over the four-week window with no sustained recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean exceeds its trailing 4-week mean despite TRANSIT remaining negative and non-recovering throughout.
